item.title: Comment on Reforming the NIH by Holden
item.description:
Reply to David Roberts:

I think you have to first ask whether the NIH is playing a valuable role in advancing medical research. I think it is. There are tremendous advances being made and I think it is risky to interfere with that progress. This smacks of making the technocratic, theoretical perfect, in some longer run end state, the enemy of the present good.

The NIH has been the preeminent institution of biomedical research in the world for many, many decades. It's not even close. In fact, it is the most successful such institution in the history of the world. The world's scientific talent comes to the US to do basic research. And the immense wealth produced by the US pharmaceutical sector is a direct outgrowth of these institutions.

You could take all of Tyler's insights and quite easily design a large additional or supplementary program that gave out grants, in the manner he suggests (faster timelines, less paperwork, less deference to seniority, more risk taking, focused on finding unconventional ideas, outside the current fads.) Then in the manner of a controlled experiment, you would compare the outcomes of this program to the existing one. Then you would allocate funds accordingly in the future.

But what we're witnessing is purely ideological, hatchet work, and all this sort of rationalizing commentary reeks of being half-hearted pretext. These people have no idea what they're destroying. How do you know? Has anybody in the whole of representative government explained why they are taking the actions they're taking other than a two word slogan "fraud and waste?" It is mindless mood-affiliation.
